1.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

1.n: he speaks to Alcinous on the evening of the second day after his arrival in Scheria; the tale of Books 9–12 was called Ἀλκίνου ἀπόλογος, 'the story told to Alcinous', as early as Plato (Merry on 9.1)

2.n: vocative of κρείων 'ruler, lord', used as an adjective

3.n: points ahead to the infinitive ἀκουέμεν

5.n: οὐ … φημι 'I say … not': 'I say there is no'
adverbial, 'at all'; accented before enclitic φημι

'realization, consummation', the highest perfection of a thing rather than its 'end', as in ἦμαρ τέλεσʼ Ἠώς 5.390; not the 'chief good' of later philosophy: Odysseus speaks of the pleasure of a feast, chiming in with Alcinous at 8.248 (Merry on 9.5)
comparative of χαρίεις 'graceful, pleasing'; predicate; the form only here in Homer

6.n: = ὅτε; with the subjunctive, of what happens at any time
in tmesis: ἔχῃ κάτα = κατέχῃ 'holds, possesses'; Merry prefers ἔχῃ intransitive, 'reigns', with κατὰ δῆμον ἅπαντα 'throughout all the people' (Merry on 9.6)
in tmesis with ἔχῃ (κατέχω 'hold, possess'), placed after the verb, accent thrown back (anastrophe)

7.n: = δώματα; plural of a single house
'listen to', + gen.; subjunctive after ὅτε (6); in Homer again only 13.9 and Iliad 4.343

8.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

9.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

10.n: epic subjunctive -ῃσι (= φορῇ); φορέω, the frequentative of φέρω: 'carries round'
uncontracted subjunctive of ἐγχέω 'pour in', as if from ἐγχείω; not the noun ἐγχείη 'spear'

11.n: second accent from enclitic τι; sums up 6–10
τοῦτό τι 'this thing, in a way': τι softens the assertion, as in σχεδόν τι, not a displaced κάλλιστόν τι (Merry on 9.11); accent from enclitic μοι

12.n: 2nd aorist middle of ἐπιτρέπω, 'turned to', + inf. εἴρεσθʼ (13): your heart is set on asking about my sorrows (Merry on 9.12)

13.n: comparative of μάλα: telling the story renews the sorrows (Merry on 9.13)

13.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

13.n: subjunctive after ὄφρα, the same in form as the indicative

14.n: adverbial; second accent from enclitic τοι
'then', merely introducing a new stage, not 'next' (Merry on 9.14); a few manuscripts have τί πρῶτον, τί δʼ ἔπειτα (Merry's critical note on 9.14)
neuter of ὑστάτιος (= ὕστατος) as adverb: 'last'
deliberative subjunctive (the form could also be future): 'tell over in order'

15.n: = κήδεα, uncontracted (Attic κήδη); object of δόσαν; the line = 7.242
emphatic: it is the number of his sorrows that makes it hard to know where to begin (Merry on 9.14)

16.n: he now grants Alcinous' request of 8.550, εἰπʼ ὄνομα (Merry on 9.1)
with the subjunctives εἴδετʼ and ἔω (17–18) (Merry on 9.17)

17.n: = εἴδετε, short-vowel subjunctive (= εἰδῆτε), after ὄφρα (16) (Merry on 9.17)
with the subjunctive ἔω (18), still after ὄφρα (16)

17.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
17.n: 2nd aorist ἔφυγον; in tmesis with ὕπο: 'escaping (from under)'; φυγὼν ὕπο νηλεὲς ἦμαρ as Iliad 21.57
in tmesis with φυγών (ὑποφεύγω 'escape'); accent thrown back after the verb

18.n: dative with ξεῖνος: 'a guest-friend to you'
epic uncontracted subjunctive (= ὦ), after ὄφρα (16) (Merry on 9.17)
plural of a single house; object of ναίων

18.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

19.n: = εἰμί, elided; not εἶμι 'go'; Virgil imitates the line, Aeneid 1.378 'sum pius Aeneas' (Merry on 9.19)
with δόλοισιν, 'tricks of every kind', as παντοίοισι δόλοισι 3.122, rather than with ἀνθρώποισι (20), as Ἀργὼ πᾶσι μέλουσα 12.70 would suggest (Merry on 9.19)
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative of cause

20.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; dative with μέλω
accusative of the goal without preposition, as κλέος οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἵκανε 8.74

21.n: for the description of Ithaca (21–27) Merry refers to his Appendix on Ithaca (Merry on 9.21)
two-termination adjective; 'clear-seen' or 'westward' (δείελος 'evening'), sense disputed, as 2.167
governs αὐτῇ at the end of the line

22.n: the mountain of Ithaca, as Iliad 2.632; Crates and Philoxenus preferred the reading Νήιον (Merry's critical note on 9.22)

23.n: uncontracted (= ναιετῶσι); intransitive, of places: 'lie, are situated'

24.n: second accent from enclitic τε; the line after 1.246
Apollodorus wrote Σάμος, here and at 1.246; Aristarchus Σάμη (Merry's critical note on 9.24)
at 1.246 the adjective has two endings, ὑλήεντι Ζακύνθῳ (Merry on 9.24)

25.n: Ithaca itself, as against the other islands (26)
'uppermost of all' (πᾶς + ὑπέρτατος), here of position at sea, 'farthest out' toward the west (πρὸς ζόφον, 26); only here in Homer

26.n: 'gloom': the dark west, where the sun sets, as 3.335; opposed to the east, πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε
contracted acc. (ἠόα > ἠῶ); πρὸς ἠῶ τʼ ἠέλιόν τε 'the east', as Iliad 12.239
epic ἠέλιος = ἥλιος; second accent from enclitic τε

27.n: two-termination adjective, used as a noun: 'rearing youths' (κοῦρος + τρέφω), like βωτιάνειρα of Phthia, Iliad 1.155 (Merry on 9.27); only here in Homer
with ἄλλο (28): 'nothing else'; accent from enclitic τοι

28.n: possessive ὅς (= ἑός), here of the speaker: 'one's own', as 34; a scholium notes that he did not say ἐμῆς, so that the saying might be more general (Merry on 9.28)

29.n: = αὐτόθι, defined by ἐν σπέσσι γλαφυροῖσι (30) (Merry on 9.29)

30.n: epic dat. pl. σπέσσι (= σπέεσι); the line = 1.15, missing in most manuscripts and probably taken from there; Wolf and most later editors reject it (Merry's critical note on 9.30)

30.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.
30.n: + inf.: 'longing (for me) to be her husband'

31.n: ὣς δʼ αὔτως 'and just so', the regular Homeric order for the later ὡσαύτως δέ (Merry on 9.31)
the goddess of Aeaea, whose story Odysseus tells in Book 10
unaugmented (= κατηρήτυε): 'held back, kept'; the object με is understood from 29

32.n: 'Aeaean', of Aeaea, Circe's island, which is itself called Αἰαίη (νῆσος) at 10.135 (Merry on 9.32)

32.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.

33.n: = ἀλλά; the line after 7.258, with the plural verb
accent from enclitic ποτε; οὔ ποτε 'never'
imperfect of an attempt that fails; subject Calypso and Circe

34.n: 'so true is it that', like Latin adeo: a general saying drawn from the instances before it, as 11.427, and οὕτως 8.167 (Merry on 9.34)
comparative of γλυκύς; + gen. of comparison
possessive ὅς (= ἑός): 'one's own', as 28 (Merry on 9.28)
used as a noun (sc. γαίης); genitive of comparison
epic gen. pl. -ήων (Attic τοκέων); genitive of comparison

35.n: 'proves to be, is'; 34–36 are marked with an obelus in some manuscripts, and Merry finds 35–36 at least suspicious, since γίγνεται spoils the form of the saying and τοκήων recurs (Merry's critical note on 9.34–36)
accent from enclitic τις; εἰ καί 'even if'

37.n: used as an interjection; εἰ δʼ ἄγε, here with the subjunctive ἐνίσπω rather than the usual imperative, as Iliad 22.381 (Merry on 9.37)
= πολυκηδέα: 'full of sorrows' (πολύ + κῆδος); in Homer only here and 23.351
aorist ἔνισπον of ἐνέπω 'tell'; hortatory subjunctive after εἰ δʼ ἄγε

38.n: with Τροίηθεν, the -θεν form serving as a genitive, as ἀπʼ οὐρανόθεν 11.18 (Merry on 9.38)
Τροίη with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word

38.p: verb · pres. part. act. dat. sg. masc.

39.n: Ἴλιος with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word

39.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

39.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with πέλασσεν; a Thracian people, allies of Troy (Iliad 2.846), on the south coast of Thrace between the Hebrus and the Lissus (Merry on 9.39)

40.n: the town of the Cicones, below the mountain of the same name; the dative is in apposition to Κικόνεσσι (39) and defines it more closely, as Κύπρον … ἐς Πάφον 8.362 (Merry on 9.39)
2nd aorist ἔπραθον of πέρθω (metathesis of -ερ- to -ρα-)
the people themselves, in strong contrast with πόλιν (Merry on 9.40)

41.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

42.n: = δασσάμεθα, unaugmented, epic -σσ- (= ἐδασάμεθα); the line again 549, its second half as Iliad 11.705
final, with the optative after a past tense
accent from enclitic τις; μή τις 'no one'
ethical dative: 'as far as I could help it', like the later ἐμοῦ γʼ ἕνεκα (Merry on 9.42)

42.p: verb · pres. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.

42.n: optative of purpose after a past tense
sc. μοίρης 'an equal share'; genitive with ἀτεμβόμενος

43.n: 'nimble'; for the disputed sense of διερός see 6.201 (Merry on 9.43); in Homer only these two places
uncontracted ἡμέας = ἡμᾶς; subject of φευγέμεν

44.n: pluperfect with imperfect sense, epic 1 sg. -εα

46.n: the subject is the companions, as of ἐπίθοντο (44) (Merry on 9.46)
contracted acc. pl. (also βόας); εἰλίποδας ἕλικας βοῦς as 1.92

47.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

47.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with γεγώνευν: the Cicones of the inland (49)
imperfect as from γεγωνέω, unaugmented, Ionic -ευν (= -ουν): 'called so as to be heard', + dat.

48.n: epic σφι(ν) = αὐτοῖς; dative with γείτονες
comparative of πολύς; epic πλέονες = πλείονες
contracted nom. pl. (= ἀρείονες); comparative of ἀγαθός

49.n: 'the mainland', inland, as against the Cicones of Ismarus on the coast (Merry on 9.49); object of ναίοντες

49.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

49.n: answered by καί (50), as κάρτιστοι μὲν ἔσαν καὶ καρτίστοις ἐμάχοντο Iliad 1.267 (Merry on 9.49)
= ἀπό; π → φ before rough breathing
'from the horses', i.e. from the war chariot, not on horseback (Merry on 9.49)

50.n: + inf. understood: the sentence is compressed; they know how to fight from the chariot, and on foot where one must (Merry on 9.49–50)
sc. τινά: 'one who is on foot', the subject of an infinitive understood (Merry on 9.50)

50.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

51.n: = ἔπειτα (τ aspirated before the rough breathing of ὅσα)
sc. ἐστί; the half-line after Iliad 2.468
singular verb with neuter plural subject
Ionic ὥρη = ὥρα; dative of time: 'in their season' (Merry on 9.51)

52.n: 'early, in the morning', predicate with ἦλθον (51); some connect it with ἀήρ, of the morning mists, others with ἦρι 'early' (Merry on 9.52)
root aorist (παρέστην), intransitive: 'stood beside', + dat. ἡμῖν (53)

53.n: 'doomed to a dread fate' (αἰνός + μόρος), as Iliad 22.481; epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); ἡμῖν αἰνομόροισιν again 24.169
= ἵνα; with the optative after a past tense
2nd aorist ἔπαθον; the subject is Odysseus and his men only (Merry on 9.54)

54.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
54.n: transitive middle, with μάχην: 'having set the battle in array', as Iliad 18.533 (Merry on 9.54)
the subject is both sides, the Cicones and Odysseus' men, hence ἀλλήλους (55) (Merry on 9.54)
object both of στησάμενοι and of ἐμάχοντο (Merry on 9.54)

56.n: ὄφρα … τόφρα (57) 'as long as … so long'; the line = Iliad 11.84, 8.66
Ionic ἠώς = Attic ἕως: here 'early day, morning'
epic ἀέξω = αὔξω; unaugmented; middle 'grow, wax': up to noon the sun's course is a rise (Merry on 9.58)

57.n: = δέ; δέ in the main clause

57.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

57.n: unaugmented (= ἐμένομεν): 'stood firm'; of Odysseus and his men (Merry on 9.54)
epic πλέονας = πλείονας; second accent from enclitic περ; the Cicones, object of ἀλεξόμενοι

57.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.

58.n: ἦμος … καὶ τότε δή (59) 'when … then'; the line as Iliad 16.779

μετά + νίσ(σ)ομαι 'go': 'passed over' the height of noon, his course now a descent (Merry on 9.58); Iliad 16.779 has μετενίσετο, and Eustathius mentions μετενείσετο and μετενίσετο as other forms (Merry's critical note on 9.58)

58.g: toward the time for unyoking oxen
58.n: βουλυτόν (βουλυτός 'the time for unyoking oxen', βοῦς + λύω) with the suffix -δε 'toward', printed as one word: late afternoon; in Homer only here and Iliad 16.779, printed there as two words (Merry on 9.58)

59.n: καὶ τότε δή 'then at last', the main clause after ἦμος (58)
unaugmented (= ἔκλιναν): 'bent back', turned to flight, as Iliad 5.37

59.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

59.n: Odysseus' men; object of κλῖναν and δαμάσαντες

60.n: indeclinable; six from each of the twelve ships (159); Crates took the number as an average of seventy-two in all, and Zoilus objected to the exact symmetry (Merry on 9.60)
= ἀπό; π → φ before rough breathing

61.n: = ὤλοντο (τ → θ before rough breathing); 2nd aorist middle 'perished'
οἱ ἄλλοι 'the rest (of us)', with the verb in the first person

62.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. pl. masc.
62.n: perfect ἀκάχημαι 'be grieved', present in sense

63.n: 'glad, well pleased'; ἄσμενοι ἐκ θανάτοιο 'glad to have escaped death', the full phrase being φύγεν ἄσμενος ἐκ θανάτοιο Iliad 20.350 (Merry on 9.63); the line again 566

63.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

64.n: 'yet, for all that': 'I let not my ships sail on, till we had thrice called to each one of our poor comrades' (Merry on 9.64)
epithet of ships: 'curved at both ends' (or 'rowed on both sides')

65.n: subject of ἀῦσαι: 'someone', distributively all the survivors, as πρίν τινα … κατακοιμηθῆναι Iliad 2.355 (Merry on 9.65)
'poor, wretched', in pity for the dead
epic ἕταρος = ἑταῖρος; partitive genitive with ἕκαστον

object of ἀῦσαι: each of the dead was called three times; the scholia explain it as an old custom of calling three times on the souls of men who died abroad, and one adds that their friends, sailing home, thought to bring them back to their own people (Merry on 9.65)

66.n: of the agent; after its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)

66.p: verb · aor. part. pass. nom. pl. masc.
66.n: contracted aorist passive of δηϊόω (δῃόω) 'cut down, slay'

67.n: epic νηυσί = ναυσί; dative with ἐπῶρσʼ: 'roused against'
= ἐπῶρσε, aorist of ἐπόρνυμι 'rouse against', + dat.

68.n: in tmesis: σὺν … κάλυψε, unaugmented (= συνεκάλυψε); σὺν δὲ νεφέεσσι κάλυψε as 5.293, again 12.314

69.n: plpf. of intransitive ὄρωρα: 'had arisen, arose'; the line = 5.294, again 12.315
οὐρανός 'sky' with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word

70.n: 'slantwise, athwart': driven on with the wind abeam, as Nitzsch takes it after Apollonius' Lexicon (πλάγιαι); Eustathius explains 'head downwards', of ships plunging their bows as they run before the wind, comparing ἐπικάρ (Merry on 9.70); only here in Homer
epic σφι(ν) = αὐταῖς, the ships; dative of possession

71.n: τριχθά τε καὶ τετραχθά 'into three and four pieces', as Iliad 3.363

72.n: epic aorist κάθεμεν (= καθεῖμεν) of καθίημι 'let down'

72.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

73.n: the ships themselves, as against their sails
from ἐσσυμένος, pf. part. of σεύω: 'eagerly, in haste'
unaugmented, epic -σσ-: 'rowed forward'; by Eustathius the reading of Aristarchus, for the common προερύσσαμεν 'dragged forward', which cannot mean rowing (Merry's critical note on 9.73)
ἤπειρον (ἤπειρος 'land') with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word

74.n: epic δύω = δύο, with the plural νύκτας
adverbial with αἰεί: 'without ceasing'; the first syllable is long because ἔχω once began with σ (Merry on 9.74), and some wrote συννεχές (Merry's critical note on 9.74)

75.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
75.n: epic ἔδω = ἐσθίω; θυμὸν ἔδοντες 'eating our hearts out', as ὃν θυμὸν κατέδων Iliad 6.202 (Merry on 9.75)

76.n: = τέλεσε, unaugmented (= ἐτέλεσε): 'brought to fullness', full daylight, not 'ended' (Merry on 5.390)

77.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
77.n: transitive middle: 'having set up'; the line nearly again 12.402 (ἱστόν)
in tmesis with ἐρύσαντες (ἀνερύω 'haul up'); acute before enclitic θʼ
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing

77.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
77.n: in tmesis: ἀνά … ἐρύσαντες 'having hauled up', where Iliad 1.480 and 4.783 have ἀνά … πέτασσαν 'spread'

78.n: 'sat (still)', while the wind and the helmsmen did the work; imperfect, the same in form as the present
'kept straight, steered'; plural with the two subjects; the line again 14.256

79.n: with the aorist indicative: what would have happened
2nd aorist; with κεν, unreal past: 'I would have come'

80.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
80.n: 'bending round' (περί + γνάμπτω 'bend'), of doubling a cape; only here in Homer

the cape at the south-east of the Peloponnese, dangerous to sailors, as 3.287, 4.514; the north-west wind caught him as he was doubling it and drove him past Cythera, when he meant to pass between the cape and the island (Merry on 9.80)

81.n: aorist ἀπέωσα (ἀπωθέω): 'thrust back'; singular with the three subjects
'drove aside, out of the course' (πλάζω 'make wander')
genitive of separation: 'away from Cythera', the island off Malea

83.n: = ἐπί; placed between noun and adjective

'teeming with fish'; Bekker and most modern editors read ἰχθυόεντα· ἀτάρ for the common ἰχθυόεντʼ· αὐτάρ, since αὐτάρ is not used in Homer with its first syllable in thesis (Merry's critical note on 9.83)
root aorist: 'set foot on', + gen. γαίης (84)

84.n: 'lotus-eaters' (λωτός + φαγεῖν); their land was a matter of doubt even in antiquity, but most placed it on or off the north coast of Africa, near the lesser Syrtis: Herodotus 4.177, Strabo on the island of Meninx (Merry on 9.80)
= τε; 'epic τε' after the relative, of what is habitual
'of flowers': vegetable food (Merry on 9.84, 'vegetable'); Bothe proposed ἀκάνθινον, after Polybius' description of the thorny lotus shrub (Merry on 9.84); only here in Homer

85.n: = ἀφυσσάμεθα, unaugmented, epic -σσ-; middle 'drew for ourselves'

86.n: unaugmented (= εἵλοντο); δεῖπνον ἑλέσθαι 'take a meal'

87.n: epic gen. -οιο; second accent from enclitic τʼ; genitive with ἐπασσάμεθʼ
= ἐπασσάμεθα, epic -σσ- (aorist ἐπασάμην): 'tasted, ate of', + gen.

88.n: imperfect as from προϊέω (= προΐην): 'sent forth'
epic by-form πεύθομαι (= πυνθάνομαι); infinitive of purpose

88.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.

89.n: οἵ τινες (= οἵτινες) 'what (men)', in an indirect question; accent from enclitic τινες

89.p: indef. rel. pron. · nom. pl. masc.

89.n: optative in an indirect question after a past tense
σῖτον ἔδοντες 'eaters of bread', used here merely to mark them as men (Merry on 9.89), as 8.222

89.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

90.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

90.n: = κήρυκα (κ → χ before rough breathing); the line again 10.102; it stands before 89 in the oldest and best manuscripts, and Ameis rejects it as interpolated from 10.102, since 94–95 imply more than three men (Merry's critical note on 9.89–90)

90.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

91.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.

91.n: unaugmented aorist passive, epic 3 pl. -εν (= ἐμίγησαν): 'mingled with', + dat.

92.n: = μήδοντο (τ → θ before rough breathing), unaugmented (= ἐμήδοντο): 'devised', + dat. of the person
epic ἕταρος = ἑταῖρος; epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν)

93.n: unaugmented (= ἔδοσαν); + inf. πάσασθαι: 'gave them to taste'
aorist ἐπασάμην of πατέομαι 'taste', + partitive gen.

94.n: epic gen. -οιο; not the clover of Iliad 2.776 but a fruit, which Herodotus (4.177) describes as the size of a mastic berry and as sweet as the date, the Lotus-eaters making wine of it too; travelers report it still eaten in North Africa, where it is called jujuba (Merry on 9.94)
aorist φαγεῖν, which serves ἐσθίω; optative in a general relative clause in past time
object of φάγοι, with the partitive λωτοῖο

96.n: unaugmented (= ἐβούλοντο); plural by sense after ὅς τις (94); with μενέμεν (97), 'would rather remain' (Merry on 9.96)

97.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
97.n: 'crop, feed on', used elsewhere of animals feeding (Iliad 2.776); here of men 'browsing' on their vegetable food (Merry on 9.97)
epic inf. -έμεν (= μένειν); the present of the lasting stay, against the aorist λαθέσθαι of the instant forgetting (Merry on 9.97)

98.n: unaugmented (= ἦγον): 'I proceeded to bring' (Merry on 9.98)

98.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.

99.n: epic νηυσί = ναυσί; 'in the ships' answers ἐπὶ νῆας (98): when he had got them there (Merry on 9.99)
with the motion of ἐρύσσας; the space under the thwarts was a safe place, where Odysseus later stows the gifts of the Phaeacians, 13.21 (Merry on 9.99)

99.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

100.n: τοὺς ἄλλους κελόμην ἐρίηρας ἑταίρους again 193
acc. pl. from a by-form ἐρίηρ

101.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. pl. masc.

101.n: epic gen. pl. (Attic νεῶν); genitive with ἐπιβαινέμεν

142.n: 'sailed in, put in to land'; only here in Homer

middle of εἶδον; infinitive of respect

145.n: οὐρανός 'sky' with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word

purpose, with the optative after a past tense

iterative -σκ-, unaugmented: 'used to tend'; the form only here in Homer

pluperfect of οἶδα with imperfect sense

'bread-eating' (σῖτος + φαγεῖν), i.e. a mortal who lives on the fruits of the earth; only here in Homer
dative with ἐῴκει (190), as ἀνδρί; a scholion calls the comparison with a wooded peak, not a mere mountain, 'an overstatement of an overstatement' (quoted by Merry on 9.192)

οἶος 'alone' (not οἷος 'such as'), predicate with ὅ

194.n: 'there, on the spot', by the ship on the shore
athematic present of ἔρυμαι 'protect, guard' (not ἐρύω 'draw'); the line again 10.444

used as a noun, in apposition

priest of Apollo at Ismarus (198); in Euripides' Cyclops (141) a son of Dionysus, while a scholion on Apollonius 3.996 makes Euanthes the son of Dionysus and Ariadne (Merry on 9.197); only here in Homer

205.n: 'unmixed, pure' (cf. ἀκήρατος); only here in Homer

οἶος 'alone, only' (not οἷος 'such as'): the three alone knew of the wine

after ὀίσατο (213); the man they would meet would want his wine strong (Merry on 9.214)

215.n: + acc. of the thing known (Merry on 9.189 cites δίκας εἰδώς here)

216.n: 'cave', used in this book beside σπέος (237); not in the Iliad

217.n: 'pasture, herd' (νομεύς 'herdsman'), + acc.; not in the Iliad

220.n: young goats; ἀρνῶν ἠδʼ ἐρίφων again 17.242, 19.398

220.n: plural: 'each group'; feminine, as μέτασσαι and ἕρσαι (221–222)

χωρὶς μέν … χωρὶς δέ … χωρὶς δʼ αὖτε, three pens by age (Merry on 9.221)

ἕρση, the same word as epic ἐέρση 'dew' (Iliad 14.351): 'dewdrops', the newly born lambs; compare Aeschylus' δρόσοι 'dewdrops' of lion cubs (Merry on 9.221)

unaugmented; from νάω 'flow' (Iliad 21.197, Odyssey 6.292), not ναίω 'dwell': 'were flowing with', + dat.; Aristarchus read ναῖον, others νᾶον, with a long α (scholia, in Merry's note and critical note on 9.222)
'whey', the watery part of milk; again 17.225; not in the Iliad
uncontracted (Attic ἄγγη); the general word, divided into γαυλοί and σκαφίδες (223) (Merry on 9.222)

223.n: 'milk-pail', probably a round bowl (Merry on 9.222); only here in Homer
'bowl', from σκάπτω 'dig, scoop' (Merry on 9.222); only here in Homer

223.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. pl. neut.

223.n: article as relative (= οἷς); dative with ἐνάμελγεν
unaugmented; 'milk into' (ἐν + ἀμέλγω), + dat.; only here in Homer

224.n: = πρώτιστα, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ἕταροι; adverbial 'first of all'
= λίσσοντο, unaugmented (= ἐλίσσοντο); + acc. of the person and infinitives (ἰέναι 225, ἐπιπλεῖν 227)

225.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. pl. masc.
225.n: 'taking', agreeing with an understood ἡμᾶς, the subject of ἰέναι: 'that we should take some of the cheeses and go back' (Merry on 9.225); a variant ἀχθομένους (Eustathius, in Merry's critical note on 9.225)

227.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. pl. masc.
227.n: agreeing with the understood ἡμᾶς (225): 'driving out … to sail'
'salt, briny'; in Homer only in the Odyssey, always with ὕδωρ (as 4.511)

228.n: with a past indicative: 'it would have been'
epic ἦεν = ἦν; with ἄν: unreal past

229.n: = ὄφρα; purpose, with the optative after the past πιθόμην (228)
'to see whether', a word like 'try' understood, as εἴ τι πόροις 267 (Merry on 9.229); accent from enclitic μοι
neut. pl. as noun: the gifts and entertainment due to a guest (at 517 'good cheer', as 5.91)

231.n: aorist ἔκηα of καίω; κήαντες apparently the reading of Aristarchus, most manuscripts κείαντες (Eustathius, in Merry's critical note on 9.231)
θύω 'offer by burning' (not θύω 'rage'): a first portion of the cheeses offered to the gods before they ate; in Homer θύω never means slaughtering a victim (Lehrs, cited by Merry on 9.231)

232.n: unaugmented (= ἐφάγομεν); the aorist φαγεῖν serves ἐσθίω
unaugmented (= ἐμένομεν); second accent from enclitic τε

'for supper' (ποτί = πρός + δόρπον): that it might serve him for light at supper, as a scholion explains; not for cooking, since the Cyclops lived on cheese and milk (Merry on 9.234); again 249, only in this book

236.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

236.n: = ἀπεσσύμεθα, root aorist middle of ἀποσεύω (σεύω 'drive', middle 'rush'), epic -σσ-: 'rushed away'
'the innermost part, the recess', as Iliad 17.36

237.n: here the ewes and she-goats he milked (238); the line again 337

238.n: epic-Ionic ἄρσην (Attic ἄρρην); neuter, μῆλα understood
epic -φι(ν) ending, here locative: 'at the door, out of doors', as θύρηφι 22.220

239.n: Ionic fem. -είης; 'deep', of a yard with high walls, as βαθέης … αὐλῆς Iliad 5.142

epic ἔκτοθεν = ἔκτοσθεν; to keep it, either αὐλή is the cave (Düntzer) or ἔκτοθεν explains θύρηφιν (238) and αὐλῆς is a genitive of place, 'in the yard' (Döderlein, Monro); Merry's text, with most editors since Bekker, prints Rumpf's conjecture ἔντοθεν 'inside the yard' (Merry on 9.235 and his critical note); again 338
the walled yard before the cave (184–186); genitive of place, 'in the fold', as the translation takes it

240.n: 'put to', closing the mouth of the cave
the stone that closes the cave (cf. θύρη 'door'); disyllabic by synizesis; in later Greek 'a long shield' (Merry on 9.240); in Homer only in this book (240, 313, 340)

240.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
240.n: 'lifting (it) high he set it in place' (Merry on 9.209 renders the phrase 'obicem magnum sursum sublatum admovit')

241.n: the door-stone; accent from enclitic γε
epic δύω = δύο, with the plural ἄμαξαι

242.n: two-termination adjective, as τετράκυκλον Iliad 24.324; Merry's text, with most modern editions, prints Barnes' τεσσαράκυκλοι, since here the ε and α would have to be lengthened (Merry's critical note on 9.242)
'heave up, lever up'; epic -σσ-, Aeolic optative -ειαν; potential with ἄν (241), as Iliad 12.448; Bekker reads ὀχλήσειαν from two manuscripts (Merry's critical note on 9.242)

243.n: two-termination adjective, always of rocks; its use of a block of stone rules out the derivation from ἥλιος and βαίνω; Buttmann, after a scholion, made it 'hard to climb', others connect λέπας 'bare rock' (Merry on 9.243)
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); plural 'doors', the cave's mouth

244.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

244.n: epic ὄϊς (Attic οἶς); acc. pl. ὄϊς, the same form as the nom. sg.
feminine adjective, of goats (cf. μηκάομαι 'bleat'), as Iliad 11.383

245.n: κατὰ μοῖραν 'in due order', as 4.783, 8.54 (Merry on 9.245)

the young after birth, not the later 'embryo' (Merry on 9.245); in Homer only in this book (245, 309, 342)
in tmesis: ὑπʼ … ἧκεν = ὑφῆκεν, set the young under the mother to suck; κ-aorist ἧκα of ἵημι

246.n: neuter used as a noun: 'the half'

246.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
246.n: 'thickening, curdling', as τρόφι κῦμα 'swollen wave' Iliad 11.307; milk was curdled with fig juice, as Iliad 5.902 (Merry on 9.246)

247.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); wicker baskets, the ταρσοί of 219 (Merry on 9.219)

247.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
247.n: middle of ἀμάω 'reap': 'gathering together' the curds: 'having curdled half the milk, he set it down in wicker baskets, having collected it together' (Merry on 9.246); a scholion's lemma has πονησάμενος μετέθηκεν, with the note that ἀμησάμενος is also read (Merry's critical note on 9.247)

248.n: purpose, with the optative after a past tense
dative of possession with εἴη: 'that he might have'

249.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. sg. masc.
249.n: agreeing with οἱ (248): 'for him to take and drink'

250.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
250.n: 'toiling, busying himself', often with an accusative (Merry on 9.250)
possessive ὅς (= ἑά), not the relative

251.n: καὶ τότε 'then', in the apodosis of ἐπεὶ δή (250)
'kindled' (ἀνά + καίω); the fire they had lit (231) had gone out or was smoldering (Merry on 9.251); πῦρ ἀνέκαιε again 308, as 7.13
unaugmented aorist εἴσιδον (= εἰσεῖδε), which serves as aorist of εἰσοράω

= πλεῖτε, elided, τ → θ before the rough breathing of ὑγρά; + acc. of the way
fem. noun with neuter plural κέλευθα; ὑγρὰ κέλευθα as Iliad 1.312

circumflexed ἦ in the second member of a double question
perfect ἀλάλημαι with present sense, 'roam about' (as Iliad 23.74)

epic ὑπείρ = ὑπέρ, lengthened for the meter
epic τοί = οἵ, article as relative; accent from enclitic τʼ
epic diectasis -όωνται (= ἀλῶνται); a variant μηχανόωνται (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 9.254)

255.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

'was broken down' (κλάω 'break'); κατεκλάσθη φίλον ἦτορ as 4.481

257.p: verb · aor. part. act. gen. pl. masc.

273.n: 'foolish, childish'; second accent from enclitic εἰς; the line again 13.237

274.n: epic infinitive -μεν of the short perfect δείδια (= δεδιέναι), with present sense

adverbial, with the comparative; ἐπεὶ ἦ πολὺ φέρτεροί εἰμεν as Iliad 20.135

epic subjunctive (= δαῶ) of ἐδάην 'learned', passive form with active sense (Merry on 9.280)

281.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
281.n: 'trying, testing', a by-form of πειράω; in Homer again 16.319, 23.114
object of λάθεν: 'he did not escape me'

281.p: verb · pf. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
281.n: agreeing with ἐμέ: 'with my knowledge of the world', as the epithet πολύμητις (Merry on 9.281)

282.n: adverbial: 'I answered him back', as 501; a scholion strangely takes it as 'the reverse of the truth' (Merry on 9.282)

284.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

284.n: epic ὑμός = ὑμέτερος ('your', of more than one): the Cyclopes' land

285.n: Ionic ἄκρη = ἄκρα 'headland'; dative with προσπελάσας

285.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
285.n: 'bringing near, driving against', + dat.; only here in Homer

286.n: 'steep', of sudden death: 'sheer'; αἰπὺν ὄλεθρον as Iliad 6.57, again 303

287.n: the line as 272, with οὐδέν for αὐτίκʼ

with ἴαλλε: 'put (his hands) on' (Merry on 9.288 joins ἐπὶ … ἴαλλε)
ἰάλλω 'send, put out', with ἐπί (as 8.443, 447); ἐπὶ χεῖρας ἴαλλε only here

289.n: in tmesis with μάρψας (συμμάρπτω 'seize together') (Merry on 9.288)

289.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
289.n: in tmesis: σὺν … μάρψας 'grasping together', as συμμάρψας Iliad 10.467; σὺν … δύω μάρψας again 311, 344
ὥς τε 'just as', introducing a comparison; accented before enclitic τε

290.n: in tmesis with ῥέε (ἐκρέω 'flow out'), as Iliad 21.119
tmesis: ἐκ … ῥέε; unaugmented, uncontracted (Attic ἐξέρρει)
unaugmented (= ἔδευε); ῥέε, δεῦε δὲ γαῖαν as Iliad 13.655, 21.119

291.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
291.n: in tmesis: διὰ … ταμών; 2nd aorist ἔταμον of τάμνω (= τέμνω)

292.n: ὥς τε 'just as'; accented before enclitic τε
'reared in the mountains' (ὄρος + τρέφω); λέων ὀρεσίτροφος as 6.130, Iliad 12.299
= οὐδέ; οὐδʼ ἀπέλειπεν is a parenthesis, 'without leaving anything', and ἔγκατα (293) depends on ἤσθιε (Merry on 9.292)

293.n: 'innards', used in the plural; second accent from enclitic τε
'full of marrow' (μυελός); only here in Homer

294.n: epic aorist ἔσχεθον (= ἀνέσχομεν), as ἀνέσχεθε Iliad 7.412: the gesture of prayer

295.n: 'cruel, unfeeling'; the vocative σχέτλιε is rendered 'Hard man' (351)

295.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

295.n: 'helplessness' (ἀ- + μηχανή 'means'); Ionic -ίη; only here in Homer
singular for the hearts of all

297.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

297.n: = ἐπί; with πίνων: 'drinking on top of it', to wash it down (Merry on 9.297 joins ἐπὶ … πίνων)
'unmixed', i.e. without water, which shows that milk was commonly diluted, or perhaps that only the whey was drunk (Merry on 9.297)

297.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

298.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

298.n: of unbroken extension through the midst, as διὰ νηὸς ἰών 12.206 (Merry on 9.298)

299.n: unaugmented (= ἐβούλευσα); + inf. 'resolve to', as Iliad 9.458

300.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

300.n: ξίφος ὀξὺ ἐρυσσάμενος παρὰ μηροῦ as Iliad 21.173 (φάσγανον 1.190)

300.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

ἤπειρον (ἤπειρος 'mainland') with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word: the Cyclopes' shore

unaugmented: 'forced, drove', + acc. and inf.; the scholia give Aristarchus' 'brought near', Callistratus' 'made' (from θεῖναι), and 'compelled'; Merry refers the word to the root θε- of θεῖναι (Merry on 9.486); in Homer only here and 542

Ionic dat. pl. -ῃς; 'oar-handle, oar' (in the Iliad the 'hilt' of a sword)

in tmesis with ὑπέκ; optative of purpose after a past tense

'immeasurable', as if 'beyond the plethron' (a measure of length); used with ἶνα

unaugmented root aorist (= ἔβημεν); in tmesis: ἐκ … βῆμεν
'surf, breakers', the line of breaking waves on the beach (cf. ῥήγνυμι)

purpose, with the optative κίοι after a past tense
